text:
Situation: Aprepitant 80 mg capsules are not on FDA's drug shortage list as of 2026-10-21. Corvale East holds 71 capsules (8.4 days), Corvale General holds 239 capsules (26.4 days), and Corvale Lakeside holds 27 capsules (16 days). Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC lists aprepitant oral powder for suspension as to be discontinued with an initial posting date of 2026-04-08.

Why (FDA record): The 80 mg capsules used at all three sites share NDC 51407070202 and label set 377c3ecb, naming Pharmathen International S. A. (FEI 3009961173) as the manufacturing plant. FDA inspected that plant on 2025-11-21 and classified the inspection OAI, with the classification known to FDA on 2026-02-26. A warning letter was issued to the firm on 2026-05-27.

Our position: Current inventory supports an internal transfer to protect Corvale East without jeopardizing other sites. No FDA shortage listing exists for the capsule formulation. External purchases carry supply-chain uncertainty because alternate labels name no identifiable plant.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 47 capsules of 80 mg from Corvale General to Corvale East — requires pharmacy director approval of the transfer request.
2. Monitor FDA shortage list and Pharmathen inspection follow-up weekly — requires buyer to report updates to the committee.

Not recommended: Purchasing from BluePoint Laboratories, Glenmark Pharmaceuticals Inc., USA, or Sandoz Inc. at this time due to unverified manufacturing sources. Transfer from Corvale Lakeside is not recommended because it yields only 9 days at Corvale East.
